title: Evidence, Observation & Diagnosis
summary: Learn to describe plant problems precisely, collect measurements, track progression, and build a differential before choosing a response.

units.title: Symptom location
units.description: Locate where a problem begins before naming a cause.

units.title: Pattern description
units.description: Use consistent language for chlorosis, necrosis, spotting, curl, wilt, and distortion.

units.title: Progression over time
units.description: Separate sudden, gradual, spreading, stable, and recovering patterns.

units.title: Measurement context
units.description: Bring pH, EC, moisture, temperature, RH, VPD, PPFD, and recent actions into the same record.

units.title: Differential workflow
units.description: Rank plausible causes and use new evidence to narrow them.

title: Seed, Germination & Establishment
summary: Follow the seed from anatomy and water uptake through radicle emergence, cotyledon transition, and common establishment failures.

units.title: Seed anatomy
units.description: Identify the seed coat, embryo, cotyledons, radicle, and micropyle.

units.title: Imbibition
units.description: Understand the first phase of water uptake and metabolic reactivation.

units.title: Radicle emergence
units.description: Follow the first visible root organ and early orientation.

units.title: Cotyledon transition
units.description: Track emergence through cotyledon opening and first true leaves.

units.title: Germination failure patterns
units.description: Separate seed viability questions from moisture, temperature, oxygen, and disease risks.

title: Roots, Rhizosphere & Water Uptake
summary: Build a root-first understanding of architecture, absorption, rhizosphere exchange, transport, and root-zone stress.

units.title: Root architecture
units.description: Map primary, lateral, fine roots, and root hairs through the occupied media volume.

units.title: Root hairs & absorption
units.description: See where short-lived absorbing surfaces develop.

units.title: Rhizosphere
units.description: Connect roots, water, ions, microbes, exudates, and oxygen.

units.title: Water & nutrient uptake
units.description: Connect substrate conditions to membrane transport and vascular flow.

units.title: Root stress
units.description: Compare low oxygen, saturation, dryback, salinity, temperature stress, and visible root decline.

title: Stems & Vascular Transport
summary: Study stem structure, xylem, phloem, internode development, and the consequences of mechanical damage.

units.title: Stem cross-section
units.description: Identify epidermal, cortex, vascular, and pith regions.

units.title: Xylem transport
units.description: Follow water and dissolved mineral movement toward transpiring shoots.

units.title: Phloem transport
units.description: Follow source-to-sink movement of photosynthate.

units.title: Internodal spacing
units.description: Relate internode length to genotype, light, temperature, stage, and growth rate.

units.title: Damage & recovery
units.description: Understand how bending, crushing, pruning, and breakage affect support and transport.

title: Branching, Training & Canopy Architecture
summary: Connect node anatomy and apical dominance to topping, low-stress training, mainlining, and screen-based canopy organization.

units.title: Node anatomy
units.description: Locate the leaf attachment, axillary bud, branch origin, and internodes.

units.title: Apical dominance
units.description: Understand how the active apex influences lateral growth.

units.title: Topping & FIM
units.description: Compare removal points and resulting redistribution of active shoots.

units.title: LST & directional growth
units.description: Use branch orientation and light exposure to redistribute canopy height.

units.title: Mainlining & SCROG
units.description: Compare structured branch selection with screen-based canopy distribution.

title: Leaves, Photosynthesis & Gas Exchange
summary: Use healthy leaves as a baseline, then connect photosynthesis, stomata, transpiration, symptom language, and inspection workflow.

units.title: Healthy leaf baseline
units.description: Establish a visual and structural reference before judging abnormality.

units.title: Photosynthesis
units.description: Connect light capture, carbon dioxide, water status, chloroplasts, and carbohydrate production.

units.title: Stomata & transpiration
units.description: Link stomatal behavior to carbon dioxide exchange and water loss.

units.title: Symptom pattern language
units.description: Describe symptoms precisely before assigning a cause.

units.title: Stomatal conductance
units.description: Go deeper into gas exchange, atmospheric demand, leaf temperature, and root-water supply.

title: Flowering, Development & Maturity
summary: Follow female flower structure from initiation through bud development, pollination response, maturity assessment, and reproductive resource allocation.

units.title: Female flower anatomy
units.description: Locate bracts, stigmas, sugar leaves, and clustered floral structures.

units.title: Flower initiation
units.description: Follow the transition from preflower expression into expanding floral sites.

units.title: Bud development
units.description: Track changes in bracts, stigmas, resin coverage, density, and senescence.

units.title: Maturity & risk inspection
units.description: Combine development, trichome observations, senescence, cultivar behavior, and mold inspection.

units.title: Reproductive source–sink transition
units.description: Understand how flowering changes demand across leaves, roots, shoots, and reproductive tissues.

title: Trichomes, Resin & Secondary Metabolism
summary: Study glandular trichome forms, anatomy, sampling, optical maturity observations, and the difference between visible resin and analytical chemistry.

units.title: Trichome types
units.description: Compare capitate-stalked, capitate-sessile, and bulbous glandular trichomes.

units.title: Gland anatomy
units.description: Identify stalk, gland head, secretory region, and storage space.

units.title: Where to inspect
units.description: Standardize representative flower-bract sampling.

units.title: Clear, cloudy & amber
units.description: Use optical condition cautiously as one maturity observation among several.

units.title: Trichome secretion & secondary metabolism
units.description: Connect gland biology to cannabinoid and terpene production without equating visible frost with potency.

title: Sex, Pollen, Seed & Breeding Foundations
summary: Learn reproductive structures, mixed-sex expression, pollen biology, seed formation, and controlled pollination workflow.

units.title: Male vs female preflowers
units.description: Compare developing staminate and pistillate structures across stages.

units.title: Mixed-sex expression
units.description: Identify anthers or staminate structures on otherwise female plants without assuming cause.

units.title: Pollen biology
units.description: Follow pollen production, release, transport, stigma contact, and fertilization.

units.title: Seed formation
units.description: Track fertilization through embryo and seed-coat development.

units.title: Controlled pollination
units.description: Use isolation, labeling, pollen handling, and recordkeeping for intentional crosses.

title: Environment, Light & VPD
summary: Treat environment as an interacting system of light, temperature, humidity, airflow, atmospheric demand, and root-zone supply.

units.title: Light distribution
units.description: Map high- and low-light zones across the canopy.

units.title: Temperature & humidity
units.description: Understand how temperature and RH combine to shape evaporative demand.

units.title: VPD & transpiration
units.description: Connect VPD to stomatal behavior, leaf temperature, water movement, and changing plant demand.

units.title: Airflow & boundary layer
units.description: Visualize the still-air boundary layer around leaves.

units.title: Supplemental lighting & DLI
units.description: Integrate natural and supplemental photons across the day.

title: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity
summary: Build an evidence-first plant-health workflow around scouting, pest and disease identification, sanitation, testing, and clean-stock practices.

units.title: Diagnostic foundations
units.description: Start every plant-health problem with location, pattern, progression, measurements, and recent changes.

units.title: Two-spotted spider mite
units.description: Identify eggs, mites, stippling, and late-stage webbing correctly.

units.title: Powdery mildew
units.description: Separate fungal colonies from residues and other pale surface material.

units.title: Hop latent viroid
units.description: Understand why laboratory testing and clean-stock practices matter for HLVd.

units.title: Pest scouting & hotspot mapping
units.description: Turn repeated scouting observations into spatial and population trends.

title: Outdoor, Protected Cultivation & Post-Harvest
summary: Connect establishment, weather, protected-environment risk, lighting, drying, water activity, and microbial quality into one applied systems course.

units.title: Hardening & outdoor establishment
units.description: Move plants into sun, wind, and changing humidity through measured acclimation.

units.title: Rainfall, irrigation & water-source integration
units.description: Connect effective rainfall, root-zone storage, runoff, irrigation, and source-water quality.

units.title: Humidity, condensation & dew-point risk
units.description: Understand condensation risk inside protected structures.

units.title: Drying temperature, RH & airflow
units.description: Treat drying as controlled moisture transfer rather than a fixed calendar schedule.

units.title: Water activity & equilibration
units.description: Separate moisture content from water activity and understand post-harvest equilibration.
